gloss: hard to stay; uncomfortable to remain (somewhere)

definitions.gloss: hard to stay; uncomfortable to remain in a place
definitions.explanation: Describes a place or situation one would rather leave — because of awkwardness, tension, or not belonging. From {居|い}る (to be somewhere) + 〜づらい (hard to do). The discomfort is social, not physical.

examples.english: I started to feel out of place there.

examples.japanese: ⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧で{居|い}づらい⟦{会|かい}→会：27493_kai⟧だった。
examples.english: It was an awkward gathering, full of people I didn't know.

examples.japanese: ⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧けんか⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{始|はじ}めた→始める：00531_hajimeru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、{居|い}づらく⟦なって→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦{先|さき}→先：02883_saki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{帰|かえ}った→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧。
examples.english: The two of them started arguing, so it got uncomfortable and I left early.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一度|いちど}→一度：01312_ichido⟧⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、⟦{職場|しょくば}→職場：04164_shokuba⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{居|い}づらくて⟦しかたがない→しかたがない：07380_shikataganai⟧。
examples.english: Ever since I made one big mistake, the workplace has been unbearably uncomfortable.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
- {居|い}づらく⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to start feeling uncomfortable staying
- {居|い}づらい⟦{雰囲気|ふんいき}→雰囲気：03604_funiki⟧: an atmosphere that makes one want to leave
- ⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{居|い}づらい: to feel unable to stay comfortably at home

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{居心地|いごこち}→居心地：06634_igokochi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{悪|わる}い→悪い：00908_warui⟧: uncomfortable to be in — very close in meaning; describes the place's effect, while {居|い}づらい describes the speaker's difficulty staying
- ⟦{気|き}まずい→気まずい：06536_kimazui⟧: awkward — about the mood between people, and does not require a place

USAGE:
The 〜⟦づらい→〜づらい：18368_zurai⟧ suffix attaches to a verb stem to mean 'hard to do': ⟦{読|よ}み→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦づらい→〜づらい：18368_zurai⟧ (hard to read), ⟦{言|い}い→言う：00515_iu⟧⟦づらい→〜づらい：18368_zurai⟧ (hard to say). It marks psychological difficulty, whereas 〜にくい more often marks practical difficulty.
